intro.title: Build bundle size guard script
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a script that checks the size of your JavaScript project's final bundle file to ensure it doesn't exceed a set limit. You'll learn how to use Node.js to read a file from the filesystem and calculate its size in bytes. The core programming concept involves using the built-in 'fs' module for file operations and conditional logic to compare sizes. By the end, you'll have a practical guard script that can be integrated into a build process to prevent large bundles from being deployed.
intro.usecase: In modern web development, monitoring bundle size is critical for performance optimization. This pattern is used in CI/CD pipelines at companies like Netflix and Airbnb to prevent performance regressions before deployment. Developers implement bundle size guards in dashboard build tools, form submission workflows, and e-commerce checkout processes to ensure fast loading times. For example, a shopping cart modal's JavaScript bundle must stay under size limits to maintain smooth user interactions during peak traffic.
